data.one_liner: Portable multi-language VM to parse, run, translate, and compile Dart, Java, Kotlin, Go, C#, JS, and Python.
data.what_it_does: ApolloVM provides a portable virtual machine for native, web, and Flutter that parses, interprets, cross-compiles, and translates code across multiple programming languages. It features on-the-fly Wasm compilation and can be used as an MCP server for LLMs.
use_when: You want an LLM MCP tool or sandboxed reasoning scratchpad to validate generated code.
You need to embed multi-language scripting in a Flutter app that updates live at runtime.
You want to compile loaded source code directly into portable WebAssembly modules on the fly.
avoid_when: You are building standard production application features that should rely on native Dart performance without a VM abstraction layer.
You need full 100% feature parity for every single control flow and operator construct across all cross-compiled languages.
strengths: Supports multiple popular source languages and translates between them.
Runs natively, on the web, and inside Flutter applications.
Compiles source code dynamically to WebAssembly without external toolchains.
weaknesses: Complex language features or specific constructs may be unsupported or limited depending on the target language and Wasm backend.
Interpreting and translating multiple languages at runtime carries significant overhead compared to native code.
data.setup_notes: Add apollovm to your pubspec.yaml dependencies.
